summary: Evaluate targeting models, fairness and data quality through applied Python analysis. Explore the five-day course outline and enrol.
lede: In social protection targeting, AI and advanced analytics help analysts and humanitarian teams assess household data for reviewable decisions. Designed for social protection analysts, programme managers and humanitarian information officers, the course covers registry-data quality, eligibility-model performance, false-positive and false-negative analysis, and subgroup fairness checks. Participants also practise documenting model limitations and decision rationale, and setting human-review pathways as data quality and response conditions change.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who analyse eligibility, coverage or vulnerability evidence and need to turn model outputs into reviewable programme decisions.
audience: Humanitarian Cash and Voucher Assistance Coordinators
prerequisites: Working familiarity with social protection targeting, humanitarian programme data or quantitative analysis is recommended. Guided Python notebook exercises include basic code interactions; prior Python experience is helpful but not required. No advanced model-development experience is expected.
topics: Data science & machine learning in practice
